extracted.intended_audience: distance education instructors, instructional designers, disability services staff, and online program administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing and delivering support services, accommodations, and experiential team-training modules for distance/online learners (including learners with disabilities). Covers identification, assessment, assistive technology, course/exam accommodations, and design principles for online team dynamics modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide individualized, disability-specific supports
rubrics_metrics.description: Online learners with disabilities require appropriate, individualized, disability-specific support services and, when required, suitable assistive technology to overcome barriers and achieve success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports should be tailored to each student's unique goals and abilities; students may receive one-time, occasional, or ongoing support depending on circumstances. Planning supports prior to enrolment is recommended to promote success and avoid later problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure web accessibility for visually impaired learners
rubrics_metrics.description: Accessible web pages are a must for learners with visual impairments who use screen-reading software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design course sites and materials to be compatible with screen readers and other accessibility tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide captioning and alternative media for hearing-impaired learners
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners with hearing impairments are unable to comprehend uncaptioned video presentations and may be unable to participate in audio-conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer captioned video, transcripts, and text-based alternatives to audio conferencing to ensure equal access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide alternatives to audio participation for communication-disordered learners
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners with hearing impairments or communication disorders (e.g., aphasia, severe stuttering) are unable to participate in audio-conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use synchronous text chat, message boards, or other text/visual channels as alternatives to audio-only activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodate fine-motor difficulties affecting keyboarding
rubrics_metrics.description: Keyboarding is difficult (or impossible) for learners with fine-motor problems or conditions such as Carpal Tunnel Syndrome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend and provide assistive-input devices (large-key keyboards, special trackballs) and adaptive software or alternative submission methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer course accommodations (time extensions and alternative formats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common course accommodations include adding extensions to the normal contract time and providing alternative formats of course materials (e.g., electronic or recorded audio versions, transcripts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: adding one or more two-month extensions to a six-month contract; provide alternative formats when materials cannot be produced on campus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer a menu of exam accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Exam accommodations involve timing modifications, assistance with presenting questions and recording answers, environmental changes, and using alternative exam formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics include deferral, additional time, breaks, larger-font exams, oral exams, use of a scribe, taking exams alone, playing relaxing music, or substituting multiple-choice with short-answer items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide and coordinate external support services
rubrics_metrics.description: External support involves provision of support from outside the university (e.g., academic strategist, interpreter, note-taker, study aide, support worker).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services may be one-time or ongoing; liaison with outside agencies and funding sources may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess assistive technology needs and support procurement/training
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess learner needs for special equipment or software (text-to-speech, word prediction, screen readers, voice input, OCR, screen enlargers) and recommend assistive-input devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services include procurement of equipment, liaison with funding sources, and training in use of assistive technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify learners through multiple pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners with disabilities are identified via (a) indication on the General Admissions Form, (b) self-referral (often via ASD web site), or (c) referral by tutor/instructor after encountering course difficulty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure multiple, accessible routes for learners to be recognized and connected with support services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comprehensive self-assessment and coordinator consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of learner support begins with a comprehensive, detailed self-assessment followed by verification and consultation with a specially trained service coordinator to determine required services and accommodations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments ascertain level of ability across functional areas and are followed by personalized planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide broad administrative supports and advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Services include information, assessment of accommodations, educational/career counselling, referrals, program planning, time-management assistance, monitoring of progress, registration assistance, funding application help, advocacy, and liaison with departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support should include both direct student-facing services and institutional liaison/advocacy functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer volunteer and ancillary assistance options
rubrics_metrics.description: Available volunteer assistance includes note taking, exam-writing assistance, mobility assistance, taping of readings, library research help, study help, tutoring, and special project help.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplement formal services with vetted volunteer supports where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a proactive approach to planning supports before enrolment
rubrics_metrics.description: Taking a proactive approach and planning disability-specific supports prior to enrolment is important to initiate a supportive environment that promotes successful learning and avoids many problems encountered after studies commence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage prospective students early to plan accommodations and reduce later barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and evaluate impact of supports on course completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing disability-specific services is associated with higher course completion rates; ongoing monitoring and evaluation of outcomes is important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use data (e.g., completion statistics) to justify and refine support services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design blended two-phase team-training (simulation + facilitated teamwork)
rubrics_metrics.description: The TDC module uses two phases: an individual, stand-alone simulation phase and a facilitated team phase using asynchronous message boards and synchronous chat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine private experiential learning with collaborative practice to develop both tacit and explicit team competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use simulations with immediate consequences to create teachable moments
rubrics_metrics.description: Simulations present time-sensitive scenarios where every learner decision has immediate consequences, creating risk of failure and teachable moments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include just-in-time feedback (an online coach) to provide positive/negative feedback; private failure encourages risk-taking and reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed team process skills into scenario design
rubrics_metrics.description: Simulation focuses on process skills: team process discussions, role assignments, leadership, conflict resolution, decision making, and planning for goal success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build scenarios from real experiences, use storytelling and multiple-path scripting to customize learning to learner choices and needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate emotional engagement and storytelling for deeper learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenarios are dramatic and encourage participation; emotions coupled with technology can produce powerful learning that stores individualized learning patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use storytelling to relate content to workplace contexts and to make learning both explicit and tacit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide preparatory facilitation to reduce technological apprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce facilitation before learners use simulation tools to minimize stress and apprehension about technology and failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early orientation and facilitator availability improve learners' comfort and later evaluations of the module.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture and build on individual reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask learners to make notes of their thoughts and feelings and provide self-evaluation tools (communication preferences, leadership style, conflict handling) to supplement the simulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these artifacts as input for later team discussions and synthesis in Phase 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish explicit chat protocols / ground rules for synchronous meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Chat protocol rules include: allow each learner to finish before responding; be patient (typing speed); avoid side conversations; signal completion/uncertainty/reactions; do not shout (CAPS); do not leave during sessions; sign on/off; keep statements brief; prepare notes ahead of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide these conduct expectations to promote orderly, inclusive synchronous interaction and equal participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design team tasks that promote continuity, consensus, and experiential conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign tasks that build on the simulation (e.g., reverse logistics plan) and emphasize consensus decision-making; facilitators introduce constraints to induce conflicting ideas so teams can experience and work through differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use realistic contingencies and surprises to force differences to the surface and create learning opportunities in conflict resolution and creativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require creation of a team-charter template
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams create a team-charter template (core activity) that acts like a checklist representing collective wisdom on formation, purpose, structure, culture, collaboration, accountability, measures of success, and deployment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask individuals to respond to charter questions then synthesize as a team; the charter governs work and social interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotate team roles to develop skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Members volunteer for and rotate roles such as leader, scribe, and timekeeper to allow for skill development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Role rotation supports development of diverse competencies across team members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support rapport-building and explicit communication planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams should meet electronically to build rapport through exchange of personal information, establish a team name/identity, set rules for engagement, plan work, and develop communication planning and coordination processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early social interaction and explicit planning help overcome lack of face-to-face cues and foster trust and participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple communication tools appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams should use chat, email, VoIP, and message boards to divide tasks, discuss ideas, and prepare summary documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide appropriate tool guidance and expectations for when and how each medium is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure active pedagogical facilitation during team work
rubrics_metrics.description: An engaged and available academic facilitator pedagogically facilitates student interaction, guides consensus processes, and introduces constraints to promote learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitator presence is crucial to manage dynamics, reduce apprehension, and scaffold difficult interactions.
